Finally, some of the key physical ideas underlying this framework, in particular, vacuum-energy contributions associated with tunnelling between topological sectors, may, in principle, be tested in laboratory experiments. A possible avenue is the search for an additional contribution to the Casimir energy in Maxwell theory, as proposed in [19–21]. This so-called Topological Casimir Effect originates from non-dispersive tunnelling contributions rather than from the conventional quantum fluctuations of propagating photons. Although such a contribution has not yet been observed, its detection would provide direct experimental evidence for the type of topological vacuum physics invoked in the present DE scenario. As emphasized in Section II C, the mechanism responsible for dark energy in this framework is tunnelling between QCD topological sectors, rather than the dynamics of a real propagating scalar field ϕ. This distinction can be represented formally by introducing an auxiliary field, the so-called Veneziano ghost; further details and references are given in Appendix B. Tunnelling contributions enter correlation functions with a sign opposite to that of a conventional propagating scalar field, such as those appearing in quintessence or k-essence models. This unusual sign is the origin of the terminology “ghost.” Crucially, however, the Veneziano ghost is an auxiliary, non-propagating field and therefore does not introduce a physical negative-norm degree of freedom or violate the usual principles of quantum field theory. Finally, the non-dispersive contact term is intrinsically infrared in origin and remains sensitive to arbitrarily large distances. In the Veneziano-ghost representation [23], the long-range topological contribution is encoded by an auxiliary, non-propagating field and manifests itself through a pole at zero momentum, q2 = 0. This should be contrasted with conventional ultraviolet contact terms, which are associated with arbitrarily short distances, x2 = 0. The topological contact term is therefore not an ultraviolet artifact and cannot be removed by the usual ultraviolet renormalization procedure; see [11] for further discussion. We conclude by noting that the possibility of longrange effects in gapped gauge theories has been recognized for some time. Lüscher [24], for example, discussed a ‘secret long-range force” in quantum field theories with instantons. Its technical origin can already be traced to the instanton analysis of ’t Hooft [25], where an infrared cutoff is required in the treatment of gauge zero modes, and the resulting corrections are power-law rather than exponentially suppressed.
